<pre class="code-block"><code>int main(void)
{
    HAL_Init();
    SystemClock_Config();
    MX_GPIO_Init();
    MX_USART2_UART_Init();

    uint8_t alert_msg[] = "[ALERT] Motion detected! Turning on light.\r\n";
    uint8_t clear_msg[] = "[INFO] Area clear. Resetting.\r\n";

    GPIO_PinState last_state = GPIO_PIN_RESET;

    while (1)
    {
        GPIO_PinState current_state = HAL_GPIO_ReadPin(GPIOB, GPIO_PIN_0);

        // Edge Detection: Only transmit when state changes!
        if (current_state == GPIO_PIN_SET && last_state == GPIO_PIN_RESET)
        {
            HAL_GPIO_WritePin(GPIOA, GPIO_PIN_5, GPIO_PIN_SET); // LED ON
            HAL_UART_Transmit(&huart2, alert_msg, sizeof(alert_msg) - 1, 100);
        }
        else if (current_state == GPIO_PIN_RESET && last_state == GPIO_PIN_SET)
        {
            HAL_GPIO_WritePin(GPIOA, GPIO_PIN_5, GPIO_PIN_RESET); // LED OFF
            HAL_UART_Transmit(&huart2, clear_msg, sizeof(clear_msg) - 1, 100);
        }

        last_state = current_state;
        HAL_Delay(50); // Debounce / sampling interval
    }
}</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="checkpoint-card">
<h4>🧪 Check Your Understanding</h4>
<p class="checkpoint-question">Why is "Edge Detection" (comparing current_state against last_state) essential when reporting sensor triggers over UART?</p>
<div class="checkpoint-options">
<div class="checkpoint-option" onclick="checkCheckpoint(this, true)">A. Without edge detection, the UART will spam hundreds of identical messages every second for as long as the sensor remains HIGH</div>
<div class="checkpoint-option" onclick="checkCheckpoint(this, false)">B. The UART hardware will burn out if left enabled</div>
<div class="checkpoint-option" onclick="checkCheckpoint(this, false)">C. The C standard library requires edge detection for strings</div>
<div class="checkpoint-option" onclick="checkCheckpoint(this, false)">D. Edge detection increases the microcontroller clock frequency</div>
</div>
<div class="checkpoint-feedback">Correct! Sensors typically remain HIGH for several seconds. Edge detection ensures you notify only on the transition from LOW → HIGH.</div>
</div>
<div class="grid-mistake-takeaway">
<div class="box-mistake">
<strong>Common Mistake</strong>
                        Using <code>sizeof(msg)</code> instead of <code>sizeof(msg) - 1</code> in <code>HAL_UART_Transmit()</code>, which transmits the invisible C null terminator <code>\0</code> over the wire!
                    </div>
<div class="box-takeaway">
<strong>Practical Takeaway</strong>
                        Always pair state change notifications with state clearing notifications so the host telemetry or cloud dashboard knows when an alarm condition has resolved.
                    </div>
</div>
</article>

<article class="scenario-card" id="scenario-19">
<div class="scenario-header">
<div class="scenario-title-area">
<h2>Firmware Update with a Bootloader</h2>
<div class="scenario-goal">Goal: Understand in-field firmware updates, VTOR vector relocation, and cryptographic security.</div>
</div>
<span class="scenario-num">Scenario 19</span>
</div>
<div class="grid-problem-observation">
<div class="box-sub problem">
<h4>⚠️ Real-World Problem</h4>
<p>An IoT product deployed on a customer's roof needs a bug fix, but opening the weather-sealed enclosure to attach an ST-LINK programmer is impossible.</p>
</div>
<div class="box-sub observation">
<h4>👀 What Student Observes</h4>
<p>The device receives a new <code>application.bin</code> over UART or Wi-Fi, validates its digital signature, flashes it to sector 4, and boots the new firmware.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="internal-box">
<h4>⚙️ What is Happening Internally</h4>
<p>Flash memory is split into two zones:
                    1. <strong>Custom Bootloader</strong> (<code>0x08000000 - 0x08007FFF</code>): Runs on reset, checks if an update is requested, downloads bytes, and verifies integrity.
                    2. <strong>User Application</strong> (<code>0x08008000</code> onward): The active product firmware.
                    To jump to the application, the bootloader re-points the <strong>Vector Table Offset Register (SCB->VTOR)</strong> to <code>0x08008000</code>, loads the application's initial MSP from <code>0x08008000</code>, and branches to the application's Reset_Handler address at <code>0x08008004</code>.</p>
</div>
<!-- Bootloader Architecture Diagram -->
<div class="visual-display-area">
<div class="visual-header">
<span class="visual-title">Dual-Stage Flash Partitioning & Boot Sequence</span>
</div>
<div style="display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:0.75rem;">
<div style="background:rgba(168,85,247,0.15); border:1px solid var(--purple); border-radius:6px; padding:0.85rem; display:flex; justify-content:space-between; align-items:center;">
<div>
<strong style="color:var(--purple);">Stage 1: Bootloader (32 KB)</strong>
<div style="font-size:0.75rem; color:var(--text-dim);">Handles update commands, CRC32 / ECDSA verification</div>
</div>
<span style="font-family:var(--font-mono); font-size:0.8rem;">0x08000000</span>
</div>
<div style="text-align:center; color:var(--blue); font-size:0.8rem; font-family:var(--font-mono);">
                            ↓ If firmware valid: Re-point VTOR & Jump to App Reset_Handler ↓
                        </div>
<div style="background:rgba(56,189,248,0.15); border:1px solid var(--blue); border-radius:6px; padding:0.85rem; display:flex; justify-content:space-between; align-items:center;">
<div>
<strong style="color:var(--blue);">Stage 2: Main Application (480 KB)</strong>
<div style="font-size:0.75rem; color:var(--text-dim);">User product logic: PIR sensor, LED controls, UART telemetry</div>
</div>
<span style="font-family:var(--font-mono); font-size:0.8rem;">0x08008000</span>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="code-container">
<div class="code-toolbar">
<span style="font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:0.8rem;color:var(--text-dim);">Bootloader Jump to Application Sequence</span>
<button class="btn-copy" onclick="copyCode(this)">Copy</button>
</div>
<pre class="code-block"><code>#define APP_START_ADDRESS 0x08008000

typedef void (*pFunction)(void);

void jump_to_application(void)
{
    uint32_t app_stack = *(__IO uint32_t*) APP_START_ADDRESS;
    pFunction app_entry = (pFunction) *(__IO uint32_t*) (APP_START_ADDRESS + 4);

    // 1. Disable all interrupts and clear pending flags
    __disable_irq();

    // 2. Relocate Vector Table to application base
    SCB->VTOR = APP_START_ADDRESS;

    // 3. Initialize Stack Pointer with application's stack top
    __set_MSP(app_stack);

    // 4. Branch to application Reset_Handler
    app_entry();
}</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="checkpoint-card">
<h4>🧪 Check Your Understanding</h4>
<p class="checkpoint-question">What is the critical difference between a CRC checksum and an ECDSA Digital Signature in firmware updates?</p>
<div class="checkpoint-options">
<div class="checkpoint-option" onclick="checkCheckpoint(this, true)">A. A CRC only detects accidental byte corruption; a Digital Signature cryptographically proves authenticity and prevents unauthorized malicious firmware from running</div>
<div class="checkpoint-option" onclick="checkCheckpoint(this, false)">B. CRC is slower than digital signatures</div>
<div class="checkpoint-option" onclick="checkCheckpoint(this, false)">C. Digital signatures require an internet connection</div>
<div class="checkpoint-option" onclick="checkCheckpoint(this, false)">D. CRC can only be computed on Linux computers</div>
</div>
<div class="checkpoint-feedback">Correct! CRC detects transmission noise. Anyone can forge a valid CRC. An asymmetric digital signature (ECDSA/RSA) requires the manufacturer's private key to sign.</div>
</div>
<div class="grid-mistake-takeaway">
<div class="box-mistake">
<strong>Common Mistake</strong>
                        Forgetting to update the linker script of the application! If the application is linked at <code>0x08000000</code> but flashed at <code>0x08008000</code>, all absolute function and vector calls will jump to the wrong memory!
                    </div>
<div class="box-takeaway">
<strong>Practical Takeaway</strong>
                        Always implement a "Rollback" dual-bank mechanism so that if a newly flashed firmware fails to boot, the bootloader automatically restores the previous working version.
                    </div>
</div>
</article>

<article class="scenario-card" id="scenario-20">
<div class="scenario-header">
<div class="scenario-title-area">
<h2>Troubleshooting Scenarios: 10 Diagnostic Lab Cards</h2>
<div class="scenario-goal">Goal: Rapidly diagnose and fix the top 10 hardware, toolchain, and firmware failures.</div>
</div>
<span class="scenario-num">Scenario 20</span>
</div>
<div class="grid-problem-observation">
<div class="box-sub problem">
<h4>⚠️ Real-World Problem</h4>
<p>Embedded systems bugs manifest as silent freezes, infinite loops in <code>HardFault_Handler</code>, or baffling electrical misbehavior.</p>
</div>
<div class="box-sub observation">
<h4>👀 What Student Observes</h4>
<p>A systematic diagnostic method separates software bugs, electrical wiring mistakes, and toolchain misconfigurations.</p>
</div>
</div>
<!-- 10 Interactive Diagnostic Cards Grid -->
<div class="troubleshoot-grid">
<!-- Card 1 -->
<div class="ts-card">
<div class="ts-symptom">🔴 1. LED Never Turns On</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Likely Causes:</strong> GPIO clock not enabled in RCC; pin set to input mode; reverse LED diode polarity; missing ground.</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Measurement:</strong> Measure voltage between pin and GND with multimeter (expect 3.3V).</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Fix:</strong> Call <code>__HAL_RCC_GPIOA_CLK_ENABLE()</code> and check anode/cathode polarity.</div>
</div>
<!-- Card 2 -->
<div class="ts-card">
<div class="ts-symptom">🟡 2. LED is Always ON (Stuck)</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Likely Causes:</strong> Active-low circuit wired to VDD; CPU stuck in infinite loop before toggle; delay is zero.</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Measurement:</strong> Attach debugger to see if PC is trapped in an Error_Handler.</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Fix:</strong> Invert logic (write <code>GPIO_PIN_RESET</code> to turn on) or fix blocking function.</div>
</div>
<!-- Card 3 -->
<div class="ts-card">
<div class="ts-symptom">⚡ 3. PIR Sensor Random Triggers</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Likely Causes:</strong> Floating input pin; PIR stabilization warm-up period not observed; noisy 5V power supply.</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Measurement:</strong> Oscilloscope shows 50Hz hum picked up on floating wire.</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Fix:</strong> Configure internal pull-down resistor (<code>GPIO_PULLDOWN</code>) and add 45s boot delay.</div>
</div>
<!-- Card 4 -->
<div class="ts-card">
<div class="ts-symptom"> 4. UART Displays Garbage Text</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Likely Causes:</strong> Baud rate mismatch; incorrect HSE/HSI clock config; missing common ground wire.</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Measurement:</strong> Measure bit-width on TX line with scope (115200 baud = 8.68 µs).</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Fix:</strong> Ensure terminal matches firmware baud rate and connect board GND to USB adapter GND.</div>
</div>
<!-- Card 5 -->
<div class="ts-card">
<div class="ts-symptom">🛑 5. Firmware Won't Start After Flash</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Likely Causes:</strong> BOOT0 pin pulled HIGH (boots into system ROM); flashed to wrong address; corrupt vector table.</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Measurement:</strong> Check BOOT0 jumper (must be connected to GND for Flash boot).</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Fix:</strong> Pull BOOT0 to GND and verify flash base is <code>0x08000000</code>.</div>
</div>
<!-- Card 6 -->
<div class="ts-card">
<div class="ts-symptom">🔌 6. Debugger Cannot Connect</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Likely Causes:</strong> Firmware disabled SWD pins (PA13/PA14); chip in deep standby sleep; loose USB.</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Measurement:</strong> ST-LINK utility reports "Cannot connect to target".</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Fix:</strong> Select "Connect Under Reset" in programmer settings and hold black NRST button.</div>
</div>
<!-- Card 7 -->
<div class="ts-card">
<div class="ts-symptom">⚠️ 7. Works in Debugger, Fails on Reset</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Likely Causes:</strong> Uninitialized global variables; debugger initializes clocks/RAM automatically; floating reset.</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Measurement:</strong> Device runs when GDB attaches, dies when powered from wall adapter.</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Fix:</strong> Ensure startup BSS zeroing loop is executing and power supply provides >500mA.</div>
</div>
<!-- Card 8 -->
<div class="ts-card">
<div class="ts-symptom">💥 8. Immediate HardFault_Handler</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Likely Causes:</strong> Null pointer dereference; unaligned 32-bit access; calling function pointer without Thumb bit set (bit 0 must be 1).</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Measurement:</strong> Read Configurable Fault Status Register (SCB->CFSR).</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Fix:</strong> Check Stack Pointer (SP) in GDB to inspect caller address in Link Register (LR).</div>
</div>
<!-- Card 9 -->
<div class="ts-card">
<div class="ts-symptom">📦 9. Bootloader BIN Doesn't Run</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Likely Causes:</strong> VTOR not updated before jump; application stack pointer invalid; interrupts not disabled.</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Measurement:</strong> Application vector table word 0 does not match RAM range (0x20000000-0x20020000).</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Fix:</strong> Set <code>SCB->VTOR = APP_ADDRESS</code> and call <code>__disable_irq()</code> prior to jump.</div>
</div>
<!-- Card 10 -->
<div class="ts-card">
<div class="ts-symptom">📏 10. ELF vs. BIN Size Discrepancy</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Likely Causes:</strong> Confusing host debugging symbols with target executable machine code.</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Measurement:</strong> Run <code>arm-none-eabi-size</code> on ELF file.</div>
<div class="ts-detail"><strong>Fix:</strong> Ignore ELF byte size on disk; use <code>text + data</code> from size output.</div>
</div>
</div>
</article>

<div class="quiz-opt" onclick="selectQuizOpt(this, 2, 3)">D. -O3</div>
</div>
<div class="quiz-explain">Explanation: Cortex-M processors only support the Thumb/Thumb-2 instruction set. Omission causes the compiler to emit 32-bit classic ARM instructions, which trigger a CPU HardFault.</div>

<div class="quiz-item" data-q="3">

<div class="quiz-opt" onclick="selectQuizOpt(this, 3, 3)">D. The baud rate was improperly set</div>

<div class="quiz-item" data-q="6">

<div class="quiz-explain">Explanation: Intel HEX uses ASCII records that self-describe destination addresses. BIN is a contiguous stream of raw memory bytes that requires supplying the target flash address (e.g. 0x08000000).</div>
</div>
<!-- Q7 -->
<div class="quiz-item" data-q="7">
<div class="quiz-item-header">
<span>7. Which register allows atomic setting and resetting of GPIO pin output bits without read-modify-write hazards?</span>
<span class="quiz-num">Q 07/10</span>
</div>
<div class="quiz-options">
<div class="quiz-opt" onclick="selectQuizOpt(this, 7, 0)">A. MODER</div>
<div class="quiz-opt" onclick="selectQuizOpt(this, 7, 1)">B. BSRR (Bit Set/Reset Register)</div>
<div class="quiz-opt" onclick="selectQuizOpt(this, 7, 2)">C. IDR</div>
<div class="quiz-opt" onclick="selectQuizOpt(this, 7, 3)">D. OSPEEDR</div>
</div>
<div class="quiz-explain">Explanation: BSRR allows setting bits in [15:0] and clearing bits in [31:16] in a single atomic bus transaction, eliminating race conditions during interrupts.</div>
</div>
<!-- Q8 -->
<div class="quiz-item" data-q="8">
<div class="quiz-item-header">
<span>8. What occurs when a digital input pin is left floating without pull-up or pull-down resistors?</span>
<span class="quiz-num">Q 08/10</span>
</div>
<div class="quiz-options">
<div class="quiz-opt" onclick="selectQuizOpt(this, 8, 0)">A. The pin defaults safely to 0 volts</div>
<div class="quiz-opt" onclick="selectQuizOpt(this, 8, 1)">B. The input has high impedance and picks up stray electromagnetic fields, toggling randomly between 0 and 1</div>
<div class="quiz-opt" onclick="selectQuizOpt(this, 8, 2)">C. The microcontroller immediately triggers a HardFault</div>
<div class="quiz-opt" onclick="selectQuizOpt(this, 8, 3)">D. The clock frequency drops by half</div>
</div>
<div class="quiz-explain">Explanation: CMOS inputs have gigohms of resistance. Without a pull resistor, ambient electromagnetic noise easily toggles the Schmitt trigger back and forth.</div>
</div>
<!-- Q9 -->
<div class="quiz-item" data-q="9">
<div class="quiz-item-header">
<span>9. In an 8N1 UART configuration at 115,200 baud, how many total physical bit durations are sent over the wire to transmit a single ASCII byte?</span>
<span class="quiz-num">Q 09/10</span>
</div>
<div class="quiz-options">
<div class="quiz-opt" onclick="selectQuizOpt(this, 9, 0)">A. 8 bits</div>
<div class="quiz-opt" onclick="selectQuizOpt(this, 9, 1)">B. 10 bits (1 Start bit + 8 Data bits + 1 Stop bit)</div>
<div class="quiz-opt" onclick="selectQuizOpt(this, 9, 2)">C. 16 bits</div>
<div class="quiz-opt" onclick="selectQuizOpt(this, 9, 3)">D. 12 bits</div>
</div>
<div class="quiz-explain">Explanation: Standard 8N1 framing requires 1 Start Bit (LOW), 8 Data bits, 0 Parity bits, and 1 Stop Bit (HIGH) for a total of 10 bit times per byte.</div>
</div>

<section class="glossary-box" id="glossary">
<h3 style="font-size:1.4rem; color:var(--text-main); margin-bottom:0.5rem;">📖 Searchable Embedded Systems Glossary</h3>
<p style="color:var(--text-muted); margin-bottom:1.5rem;">Instant reference definitions for key toolchain, ARM Cortex-M, and peripheral terms.</p>
<input class="glossary-search" id="glossary-filter" onkeyup="filterGlossary()" placeholder="Search glossary (e.g., ELF, Linker, VTOR, BSRR, SysTick, NVIC)..." type="text"/>
<div class="glossary-grid" id="glossary-container">
<div class="glossary-item">
<dt>Preprocessor</dt>
<dd>Initial toolchain stage that performs textual inclusion of header files (#include) and macro substitution (#define) before C compilation.</dd>
</div>
<div class="glossary-item">
<dt>Compiler (cc1)</dt>
<dd>Translates high-level C code into target-specific assembly language instructions for the ARM Cortex-M architecture.</dd>
</div>
<div class="glossary-item">
<dt>Assembler (as)</dt>
<dd>Converts human-readable assembly instructions (LDR, STR, MOV) into raw binary relocatable machine opcodes in an object file (.o).</dd>
</div>
<div class="glossary-item">
<dt>Linker (ld)</dt>
<dd>Combines multiple object files, resolves function symbols, and binds sections to physical memory addresses based on a linker script.</dd>
</div>
<div class="glossary-item">
<dt>Linker Script (.ld)</dt>
<dd>Configuration file defining physical memory regions (FLASH, RAM) and dictating where code (.text), constants (.rodata), and data (.data, .bss) sit.</dd>
</div>
<div class="glossary-item">
<dt>ELF (Executable & Linkable Format)</dt>
<dd>Standard structured binary file format containing machine code, section headers, symbol tables, and DWARF debugging information.</dd>
</div>
<div class="glossary-item">
<dt>DWARF</dt>
<dd>Standardized debugging data format embedded in ELF files that allows GDB to map memory addresses back to specific C source file lines and variable names.</dd>
</div>
<div class="glossary-item">
<dt>Intel HEX (.hex)</dt>
<dd>ASCII text representation of binary data where each line is a record containing byte counts, 32-bit memory addresses, data, and checksums.</dd>
</div>
<div class="glossary-item">
<dt>Raw Binary (.bin)</dt>
<dd>Contiguous binary stream of executable bytes with zero headers or address metadata, flashed directly to a known starting offset.</dd>
</div>
<div class="glossary-item">
<dt>Vector Table</dt>
<dd>Array of 32-bit exception and interrupt handler function pointers located at base memory (0x08000000) whose first entry is the initial Stack Pointer.</dd>
</div>
<div class="glossary-item">
<dt>Reset_Handler</dt>
<dd>The first assembly function executed by the Cortex-M processor upon release of reset; copies .data to RAM, zeros .bss, and calls main().</dd>
</div>
<div class="glossary-item">
<dt>Main Stack Pointer (MSP)</dt>
<dd>Hardware register (SP / R13) holding the memory address of the current stack frame, automatically loaded from address 0x08000000 at power-on.</dd>
</div>
<div class="glossary-item">
<dt>Program Counter (PC)</dt>
<dd>CPU register (R15) holding the memory address of the current instruction being fetched and executed.</dd>
</div>
<div class="glossary-item">
<dt>BSRR (Bit Set/Reset Register)</dt>
<dd>Dedicated 32-bit GPIO register allowing atomic setting and clearing of output pins without read-modify-write race conditions.</dd>
</div>
<div class="glossary-item">
<dt>EXTI (Extended Interrupts Controller)</dt>
<dd>STM32 hardware peripheral monitoring GPIO pin state transitions (rising/falling edges) and routing interrupt requests to the NVIC.</dd>
</div>
<div class="glossary-item">
<dt>NVIC</dt>
<dd>Nested Vectored Interrupt Controller: on-core ARM hardware managing interrupt priorities, nesting, and sub-12-cycle low-latency ISR pre-emption.</dd>
</div>
<div class="glossary-item">
<dt>UART / USART</dt>
<dd>Universal Asynchronous Receiver-Transmitter: serial communication peripheral transmitting 8N1 bit-streams using fixed baud rate timing.</dd>
</div>
<div class="glossary-item">
<dt>PIR Sensor</dt>
<dd>Passive Infrared Sensor: pyroelectric sensor detecting changes in thermal radiation caused by human movement, driving a digital GPIO HIGH.</dd>
</div>
<div class="glossary-item">
<dt>VTOR</dt>
<dd>Vector Table Offset Register in the System Control Block (SCB) allowing software to dynamically relocate the interrupt vector table to RAM or an application offset.</dd>
</div>
<div class="glossary-item">
<dt>SWD (Serial Wire Debug)</dt>
<dd>Two-wire debug protocol (SWDIO and SWCLK) replacing JTAG to flash microcontrollers and inspect CPU registers via hardware debug probes.</dd>
</div>
</div>
</section>

<div class="tree-map"><span class="branch">Build Tools Pipeline</span>

├── <span class="leaf">Linker (ld)</span>        : Symbol resolution & memory mapping using linker script (.ld)

<span class="branch">Binary Firmware Artifacts</span>
├── <span class="leaf">Object File (.o)</span>   : Relocatable machine code with unresolved symbol tables (nm)
├── <span class="leaf">ELF File (.elf)</span>    : Complete package: code + data + symbols + DWARF debug info
├── <span class="leaf">Intel HEX (.hex)</span>   : Self-addressed ASCII records with longitudinal checksums

<span class="branch">Hardware Power-On & Reset Sequence</span>
├── <span class="leaf">Power-On Reset</span>     : Voltage stabilizes > POR threshold (~1.7V), reset line released
├── <span class="leaf">0x08000000</span>         : Hardware loads Word 0 into Main Stack Pointer (MSP)
├── <span class="leaf">0x08000004</span>         : Hardware loads Word 1 into Program Counter (PC ← Reset_Handler)
├── <span class="leaf">Reset_Handler</span>      : Copies .data from Flash to RAM, zeros .bss in RAM
├── <span class="leaf">SystemInit()</span>       : Initializes clock tree (PLL/HCLK), enables FPU coprocessor

├── <span class="leaf">GPIO Input</span>         : PIR sensor thermal trigger → Schmitt Trigger → IDR register
├── <span class="leaf">Interrupt Control</span>  : Pin edge → EXTI → NVIC hardware stacking → ISR callback
├── <span class="leaf">GPIO Output</span>        : BSRR atomic register → Push-Pull MOSFETs → 3.3V LED drive
└── <span class="leaf">UART Serial</span>        : Shift register transmits 8N1 bit-stream at 115,200 baud to terminal</div>

}`;
            } else {
                btn.textContent = 'Show Simplified View';
                lbl.textContent = 'Preprocessed Output: main.i (Full Expansion Snippet)';
                out.textContent = `// # 1 "main.c"
// # 1 "<built-in>"
// # 1 "<command-line>"
// # 1 "Drivers/CMSIS/Device/ST/STM32F4xx/Include/stm32f4xx.h" 1
typedef enum { ... } IRQn_Type;
# 250 "Drivers/STM32F4xx_HAL_Driver/Inc/stm32f4xx_hal.h"
typedef struct {
  volatile uint32_t CR;
  volatile uint32_t PLLCFGR;
  ... 14,800 more lines ...
} RCC_TypeDef;
// [Comments stripped, macros substituted directly into tokens]`;
            }
        }

        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        // 6. Scenario 4: Assembly Stepper Animation
        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        let currentAsmStep = 0;
        function stepAsmAnimation() {
            const steps = document.querySelectorAll('#asm-steps-box .asm-step');
            steps.forEach(s => {
                s.style.borderLeftColor = 'transparent';
                s.style.background = 'transparent';
            });
            currentAsmStep = (currentAsmStep + 1) % steps.length;
            steps[currentAsmStep].style.borderLeftColor = 'var(--blue)';
            steps[currentAsmStep].style.background = 'rgba(56,189,248,0.1)';
        }

        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        // 7. Scenario 7: ELF Inspector
        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        const elfInfo = {
            header: {
                desc: "The ELF Header defines 32-bit ARM Little-Endian architecture, ABI version, entry point (0x08000189), and table offsets.",
                dest: "Read by host GDB and flashing software; NOT burned into microcontroller flash.",
                cmd: "arm-none-eabi-readelf -h firmware.elf"
            },
            progheader: {
                desc: "Program Headers specify loadable segments (LOAD), permissions (Read/Write/Execute), Flash physical offsets, and RAM virtual addresses.",
                dest: "Parsed by STM32CubeProgrammer to determine where flash blocks are burned.",
                cmd: "arm-none-eabi-readelf -l firmware.elf"
            },
            text: {
                desc: ".text holds compiled machine code instructions; .rodata holds const strings, lookup tables, and literal numbers.",
                dest: "Burned into STM32 NOR Flash memory starting at 0x08000400.",
                cmd: "arm-none-eabi-objdump -d firmware.elf"
            },
            data: {
                desc: ".data contains initial values for initialized variables; .bss defines size of zero-initialized variables.",
                dest: ".data LMA in Flash, VMA in RAM; .bss reserved exclusively in RAM.",
                cmd: "arm-none-eabi-readelf -S firmware.elf"
            },
            symtab: {
                desc: "Symbol Table (.symtab) maps function and global variable names to exact 32-bit memory addresses.",
                dest: "Used by GDB on PC to resolve variable and function names; stripped before flashing.",
                cmd: "arm-none-eabi-nm -n firmware.elf"
            },
            debug: {
                desc: "DWARF Debug sections (.debug_info, .debug_line) map machine instructions to exact C source line numbers.",
                dest: "Lives exclusively on host computer; enables source-level breakpoints and stepping in GDB.",
                cmd: "arm-none-eabi-readelf --debug-dump=line firmware.elf"
            }
        };

        function inspectElf(key) {
            const info = elfInfo[key];
            if (!info) return;

            document.querySelectorAll('#elf-blocks .pipeline-step').forEach(b => b.classList.remove('active'));
            event.currentTarget.classList.add('active');

            document.getElementById('elf-desc').textContent = info.desc;
            document.getElementById('elf-dest').textContent = info.dest;
            document.getElementById('elf-cmd').textContent = info.cmd;
        }

        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        // 8. Scenario 10: Reset Timeline Stepper
        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        let timelineIdx = 0;
        function stepTimeline() {
            const items = document.querySelectorAll('#timeline-list .checkpoint-option');
            items.forEach(i => i.classList.remove('correct'));
            timelineIdx = (timelineIdx + 1) % items.length;
            items[timelineIdx].classList.add('correct');
        }

        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        // 9. Scenario 11: RAM State Before/After Toggle
        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        let ramStateClean = false;
        function toggleRamState() {
            ramStateClean = !ramStateClean;
            const btn = document.getElementById('ram-toggle-btn');
            const lbl = document.getElementById('ram-state-label');
            const cells = document.getElementById('ram-cells');

            if (ramStateClean) {
                btn.textContent = 'Reset to Power-On State';
                lbl.textContent = 'RAM State: AFTER Startup Initialization';
                cells.innerHTML = `
                    <div style="color:var(--green);">0x20000000 (.data): <strong>0x0000000A</strong> (counter = 10 COPIED)</div>
                    <div style="color:var(--green);">0x20000004 (.data): <strong>0x42494F53</strong> (magic = 0x4249... COPIED)</div>
                    <div style="color:var(--green);">0x20000008 (.bss) : <strong>0x00000000</strong> (total = 0 ZEROED)</div>
                `;
            } else {
                btn.textContent = 'Run Startup Copy Loop';
                lbl.textContent = 'RAM State: BEFORE Startup (Power-on Garbage)';
                cells.innerHTML = `
                    <div style="color:var(--red);">0x20000000 (.data): <strong>0xA5C3F012</strong> (GARBAGE)</div>
                    <div style="color:var(--red);">0x20000004 (.data): <strong>0x77EE1122</strong> (GARBAGE)</div>
                    <div style="color:var(--red);">0x20000008 (.bss) : <strong>0xDEADBEEF</strong> (GARBAGE)</div>
                `;
            }
        }

        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        // 10. Scenario 12: CPU Fetch-Decode-Execute Stepper
        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        const cpuCycles = [
            { pc: "0x08000200", opcode: "0x4803 (LDR)", decode: "ldr r0, [pc, #12]", exec: "r0 <- 0x40020000 (GPIOA Base)" },
            { pc: "0x08000202", opcode: "0x6941 (LDR)", decode: "ldr r1, [r0, #0x14]", exec: "r1 <- Read GPIOA_ODR (0x0000)" },
            { pc: "0x08000204", opcode: "0xF081 (EOR)", decode: "eor r1, r1, #32", exec: "r1 <- 0x0020 (Bit 5 inverted)" },
            { pc: "0x08000208", opcode: "0x6141 (STR)", decode: "str r1, [r0, #0x14]", exec: "GPIOA_ODR <- 0x0020 (Pin HIGH!)" }
        ];
        let cpuCycleIdx = 0;

        function stepCpuCycle() {
            cpuCycleIdx = (cpuCycleIdx + 1) % cpuCycles.length;
            const c = cpuCycles[cpuCycleIdx];
            document.getElementById('cpu-pc-val').textContent = c.pc;
            document.getElementById('cpu-opcode-val').textContent = c.opcode;
            document.getElementById('cpu-decode-val').textContent = c.decode;
            document.getElementById('cpu-exec-val').textContent = c.exec;
        }

        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        // 11. Scenario 14: PIR Motion Simulation
        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        let pirActive = false;
        function triggerPirMotion() {
            pirActive = true;
            const lens = document.getElementById('pir-lens');
            const state = document.getElementById('pir-state-text');
            const label = document.getElementById('pir-wave-label');
            const feedback = document.getElementById('pir-feedback-text');

            if (lens && state) {
                lens.setAttribute('opacity', '0.9');
                lens.setAttribute('fill', '#ef4444');
                state.textContent = 'OUT: HIGH (3.3V) - MOTION!';
                state.style.color = '#ef4444';
                if (label) label.textContent = 'MOTION ACTIVE (3.3V)';
                if (feedback) feedback.textContent = 'Status: Pyroelectric crystal saturated! Pin PB0 driven HIGH for 3 seconds.';

                setTimeout(() => {
                    lens.setAttribute('opacity', '0.3');
                    lens.setAttribute('fill', '#38bdf8');
                    state.textContent = 'OUT: LOW (0.0V)';
                    state.style.color = 'var(--text-muted)';
                    if (label) label.textContent = 'IDLE (0.0V)';
                    if (feedback) feedback.textContent = 'Status: Waiting for infrared disturbance. Click "Simulate Motion" to trigger.';
                    pirActive = false;
                }, 3000);
            }
        }

        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        // 12. Scenario 16: UART Bit Animation
        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        function animateUartBits() {
            const status = document.getElementById('uart-sim-status');
            if (status) {
                status.textContent = 'Transmitting: [Start=0] -> [1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0] -> [Stop=1] @ 115200 baud... DONE (Byte 0x4D received)';
                status.style.color = 'var(--green)';
                setTimeout(() => {
                    status.textContent = 'Format: 1 Start Bit (0) • 8 Data Bits (LSB First) • No Parity • 1 Stop Bit (1) • Idle State = 3.3V HIGH';
                    status.style.color = 'var(--text-dim)';
                }, 3500);
            }
        }

        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        // 13. Scenario 17: Integrated Full Lab Workbench
        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        function clearTerminal() {
            const term = document.getElementById('serial-terminal');
            if (term) {
                term.innerHTML = `
                    <div class="terminal-header">
                        <span>PORT: /dev/tty.usbmodem14103 (ST-LINK VCP)</span>
                        <span>BAUD: 115200</span>
                    </div>
                    <div style="color:#64748b;">[Console Cleared]</div>
                `;
            }
        }

        function triggerFullDemo() {
            const pirLed = document.getElementById('bench-pir-led');
            const pirDesc = document.getElementById('bench-pir-desc');
            const userLed = document.getElementById('bench-user-led');
            const ledDesc = document.getElementById('bench-led-desc');
            const uartTx = document.getElementById('bench-uart-tx');
            const term = document.getElementById('serial-terminal');

            // 1. PIR Detects motion
            pirLed.style.background = '#38bdf8';
            pirLed.style.boxShadow = '0 0 10px #38bdf8';
            pirDesc.textContent = 'State: MOTION DETECTED (HIGH)';

            // 2. MCU turns LED ON
            userLed.style.background = '#10b981';
            userLed.style.boxShadow = '0 0 10px #10b981';
            ledDesc.textContent = 'State: ON (3.3V)';

            // 3. UART transmits
            uartTx.textContent = 'TX: TRANSMITTING...';
            uartTx.style.color = 'var(--amber)';

            const now = new Date().toTimeString().split(' ')[0];
            const line = document.createElement('div');
            line.style.color = '#38bdf8';
            line.textContent = `[${now}] [ALERT] Motion detected! Turning on light.`;
            term.appendChild(line);
            term.scrollTop = term.scrollHeight;

            setTimeout(() => {
                uartTx.textContent = 'TX: IDLE';
                uartTx.style.color = 'var(--text-dim)';
            }, 800);

            // 4. Auto reset after 3.5 seconds
            setTimeout(() => {
                pirLed.style.background = '#475569';
                pirLed.style.boxShadow = 'none';
                pirDesc.textContent = 'State: IDLE (LOW)';

                userLed.style.background = '#475569';
                userLed.style.boxShadow = 'none';
                ledDesc.textContent = 'State: OFF (0V)';

                const lineClear = document.createElement('div');
                lineClear.style.color = '#94a3b8';
                const clearTime = new Date().toTimeString().split(' ')[0];
                lineClear.textContent = `[${clearTime}] [INFO] Area clear. Resetting.`;
                term.appendChild(lineClear);
                term.scrollTop = term.scrollHeight;
            }, 3500);
        }

        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        // 14. Checkpoints (Scenario Quizzes)
        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        function checkCheckpoint(opt, isCorrect) {
            const card = opt.closest('.checkpoint-card');
            const allOpts = card.querySelectorAll('.checkpoint-option');
            const feedback = card.querySelector('.checkpoint-feedback');

            allOpts.forEach(o => {
                o.classList.remove('correct', 'incorrect');
                o.style.pointerEvents = 'none';
            });

            if (isCorrect) {
                opt.classList.add('correct');
                feedback.style.display = 'block';
                feedback.style.background = 'rgba(16,185,129,0.15)';
                feedback.style.color = 'var(--green)';
                feedback.style.border = '1px solid var(--green)';
            } else {
                opt.classList.add('incorrect');
                allOpts.forEach(o => {
                    if (o.getAttribute('onclick').includes('true')) o.classList.add('correct');
                });
                feedback.style.display = 'block';
                feedback.style.background = 'rgba(239,68,68,0.15)';
                feedback.style.color = 'var(--red)';
                feedback.style.border = '1px solid var(--red)';
            }
        }

        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        // 15. Final 10-Question Assessment
        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        const quizAnswers = {
            1: 1, // B
            2: 1, // B
            3: 0, // A
            4: 1, // B
            5: 0, // A
            6: 1, // B
            7: 1, // B
            8: 1, // B
            9: 1, // B
            10: 1 // B
        };

        const userSelections = {};

        function selectQuizOpt(opt, qNum, optIdx) {
            userSelections[qNum] = optIdx;
            const parent = opt.closest('.quiz-options');
            parent.querySelectorAll('.quiz-opt').forEach(o => o.classList.remove('selected'));
            opt.classList.add('selected');
        }

        function submitFinalQuiz() {
            let score = 0;
            for (let q = 1; q <= 10; q++) {
                const item = document.querySelector(`.quiz-item[data-q="${q}"]`);
                const options = item.querySelectorAll('.quiz-opt');
                const explain = item.querySelector('.quiz-explain');
                const correctIdx = quizAnswers[q];
                const selectedIdx = userSelections[q];

                options.forEach((opt, idx) => {
                    opt.style.pointerEvents = 'none';
                    if (idx === correctIdx) {
                        opt.classList.add('result-correct');
                    } else if (idx === selectedIdx) {
                        opt.classList.add('result-wrong');
                    }
                });

                if (selectedIdx === correctIdx) {
                    score++;
                }
                explain.style.display = 'block';
            }

            const scoreCard = document.getElementById('final-score-card');
            const scoreDisplay = document.getElementById('final-score-display');
            const feedbackMsg = document.getElementById('final-feedback-msg');

            scoreDisplay.textContent = `${score} / 10`;
            scoreCard.style.display = 'block';

            if (score >= 9) {
                feedbackMsg.textContent = "Outstanding Mastery! You possess deep systems-level intuition for ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers, toolchains, memory architecture, and peripheral interfaces.";
                scoreDisplay.style.color = "var(--green)";
            } else if (score >= 7) {
                feedbackMsg.textContent = "Solid Understanding! Review the questions with detailed explanations above to master linker scripts, bootloader vector relocation, and UART framing.";
                scoreDisplay.style.color = "var(--blue)";
            } else {
                feedbackMsg.textContent = "Good effort! Review Scenarios 6 (Linker scripts), 10 (Reset sequence), and 15 (Interrupts) to solidify your embedded firmware foundation.";
                scoreDisplay.style.color = "var(--amber)";
            }

            scoreCard.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth' });
        }

        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        // 16. Searchable Glossary Filter
        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        function filterGlossary() {
            const input = document.getElementById('glossary-filter').value.toLowerCase();
            const items = document.querySelectorAll('#glossary-container .glossary-item');

            items.forEach(item => {
                const term = item.querySelector('dt').textContent.toLowerCase();
                const desc = item.querySelector('dd').textContent.toLowerCase();
                if (term.includes(input) || desc.includes(input)) {
                    item.style.display = 'block';
                } else {
                    item.style.display = 'none';
                }
            });
        }

        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        // 17. Scroll Spy & Progress Bar Tracking
        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        window.addEventListener('scroll', () => {
            const winScroll = document.documentElement.scrollTop || document.body.scrollTop;
            const height = document.documentElement.scrollHeight - document.documentElement.clientHeight;
            const scrolled = (winScroll / height) * 100;
            const progressFill = document.getElementById('progress-fill');
            if (progressFill) progressFill.style.width = scrolled + '%';

            // Update Active Scenario in Sidebar
            const scenarios = document.querySelectorAll('.scenario-card');
            const navItems = document.querySelectorAll('.scenario-list .scenario-item');

            let currentId = '';
            scenarios.forEach(sc => {
                const top = sc.offsetTop - 120;
                if (winScroll >= top) {
                    currentId = sc.getAttribute('id');
                }
            });

            navItems.forEach(item => {
                const link = item.querySelector('a');
                if (link && link.getAttribute('href') === '#' + currentId) {
                    item.classList.add('active');
                } else {
                    item.classList.remove('active');
                }
            });
        });
    </script>
